title: Policy & Procedure for Confidentiality, Integrity and Security of Information
html:
POLICY & PROCEDURE

ON CONFIDENTIALITY, INTEGRITY, SECURITY OF RECORDS

  • PURPOSE:
    • To protect the medical records from any damage / tamper unauthorized use.
    • Medical / departmental records and information regarding patients / company matters are legally protected for protection of privacy.
  • SCOPE:

Hospital wide - All Patient care areas

  • RESPONSIBILITY:

All care providers

  • ABBREVIATIONS:
    • HMIS:Hospital Management Information System
    • IA:Initial Assessment
    • ICU:Intensive Care Unit
    • IMS:Information Management System
    • IP:Indoor Patient
    • IT:Information Technology
    • MLC:Medico-Legal Case
    • MR:Medical Records
    • MRD:Medical Records Department
    • NABH:National Accreditation Board For Hospitals and Healthcare Providers
    • OP:Outdoor Patient
    • SOP:Standard Operating Procedures
    • TPA:Third Party Assurance
    • UHID:Unique Hospital Identification Number
  • DEFINITIONS:
    • Confidentiality:

Restricted access to information to individuals who have a need, a reason and permission for such access.

It also includes an individual’s right to personal privacy as well as privacy of information related to his / her health care records. All documents to be kept in lock & key.

    • Security:

Protection from loss, destruction, tampering and unauthorized access or use

    • Integrity:

Protecting information from accidental or unauthorized intentional change

    • Information Browsing:

Viewing of information by unauthorized or legitimate user

  • REFERENCE:
    • NABH: NABH Standards for Hospitals
  • POLICY:
    • The MRD shall apply various methods and tools to prevent any damage / tampering to the medical records occurring due misplacement, pests, fire or any other factor.
    • The medical records are strictly confidential and may be released only by consent of the patient or by an authorization letter duly signed by the patient. This written consent is necessary before any information from patient’s medical record is shared with any organization, prospective employer, insurance company or other individual(s).
    • Hospital shall maintain the Confidentiality, Security and Integrity of Medical Records as per the procedure for maintaining Confidentiality, Security and Integrity of data.
    • Policies complied with Indian penal code and Code of Medical Ethics.
    • The details in the medical record shall not be disclosed to anyone except the care providers, Patients and court of law.
    • Any part of Medical record shall not be reproduced.
    • The access to medical records department shall be limited to the Medical Director, Administrator, Medical Records Officer and the Quality Assurance committee of the hospital.
    • The consultants who are in need of Medical records for research purpose shall be given the same after getting necessary authorization from management, record of which is maintained.
    • Medical records shall be issued to the authorized persons after making entry in the register, a record of photo I.D. is taken along with an application.
    • All the Case sheets shall be stored in an environment with adequate pest and rodent control measures.
    • The MLC Records shall be stored under lock and key.
    • The Medical records are given to the Physician, Patients and Other Public Agencies as per the laid down procedure.
    • Photo copies of the records shall be furnished to the TPA parties and Income Tax authorities after approval from the Administrator.
  • PROCEDURE:
    • General Protocols:
      • Any corrections will be made in the Medial Records after getting proper proof and affidavit from the notary.
      • Only authorized staff members and care providers have access to patient’s medical record.
      • Access of medical records by a parent differs depending upon patient’s age.
      • If patient is eighteen (18) or older, parents have no access to patient’s medical record without his / her permission.
      • In most cases, if patient is seventeen (17) or younger, his / her parents can have access to the medical records.
      • The privileged health information is not disclosed without the patient’s authorization except in following cases:
        • It is asked to be produced in the court of law as evidence in a trial;
        • Under oath of parliament; In communities interest;
        • In the interest of doctors; if asked by medical audit committee or quality assessment committee.
      • They can access patient medical records as reasonable necessary to evaluate or review the diagnosis or treatment, to evaluate or improve the quality of health care rendered, to determine the health care services rendered were performed in compliance with the applicable standard of care.
      • Doctors are authorized to access the medical records of patients whom they are presently treating or as reasonably necessary to provide follow-up care, including review to determine medical protocol of prior patients.
      • Every access shall be made by doctors with the help of a requisition slip duly signed by the doctor.
      • The X-Ray Films will be issued to patients after consultant’s approval.
      • A grant of access or release of a written medical record does not authorize any further dissemination of the record to any other person unless authorized in writing by the patient.
      • The registered medical practitioner cannot disclose the secrets of a patient that have been learnt during exercise of his/her profession except:
        • In a court of law under orders of the presiding judge;
        • In circumstances where there is a serious and identified risk to a specific person and or community;
        • Notifiable diseases: In case of communicable / notifiable diseases, concerned public health authorities should be informed immediately.
      • Consents to release shall be maintained as part of the medical record.
      • Records of persons who have accessed a medical record shall be maintained as the property of the medical record.
    • Procedure to ensure confidentiality, security and integrity of data:
      • The Medical Record is a private document related to the patient history and treatment both in a physical and electronic format and should not be disclosed as it breaches the Code of Medical Ethics.
      • No part of the information contained in the MR should be reproduced in any format by any individual who is handling the contents or details of the patient record without the consent of the management and the patient concerned unless otherwise needed for any case of subpoena or any other legal proceedings the information may be presented before the actual trial of cases without the consent of the patient.
      • Only the people authorized by the management have the right to access the patient information in the electronic medical records.
      • This is controlled by the password control and the access level given to each individual on the EMR.
      • Based on the profile of the personnel the authorization levels vary from only viewing the records to making entries and altering the records of the patient.
      • Only on written consent / authorization from the patient / legal heirs and an authorization from the management can the information be released to any external individual.
      • The access to the Records by the visiting doctors should be provided once the doctor has been referred by the main treating doctor; the case sheets are available in the nurse’s station.
      • No record will be issued to any authority after discharge of patient after then hospital staff authorized by management, without a requisition duly signed by authority along with a photo I.D. and approval from the Administrator. The same is than kept with original record of the patients for future reference.
    • Procedure for safeguarding data against loss, destruction and tampering:
      • All the records are placed in a safe and secure environment with the controlled access to the department. No external individual (who are not part of the top management, MR team or the Quality team) shall be allowed inside the department without proper authorization letter from the management.
      • The room is sealed off after its working time and it is air conditioned to ensure safety of records.
      • Pest and rodent control measures are periodically carried out to ensure safe storage of records.
      • The records shall be taken a back-up once in fifteen days. It is the responsibility of the IT department to ensure adequate back up of records in case of unexpected events like system crash, virus attack or any other damages.
      • Totally, three backup copies are maintained; one at the department, one with the management and the other at the Director’s Office.
      • It is the responsibility of the IT department to restrict access to records once closed through issuing passwords to different users restricting their access to different modules in the system, regularly conduct an audit on the system access by different users.
    • Response to patients:
      • The patients who are in need of the Medical record shall submit the requisition with approval from the Administrator.
      • After submission of the requisition, the photocopy of the Medical Record is given after getting signature photo I.D. in the appropriate register.
      • In case the patient attendant asks for the MR, an authorization letter from the patient shall be submitted with the requisition duly signed & photo I.D.by the Administrator.
      • Both requisition and photo I.D. are kept with M.R. of the patient.
    • Response to the physicians:
      • If the Doctors other than the Care provider of the patient ask for the MR, requisition form filled in by them with signature from the Administrator shall be submitted.
      • The photocopy of the Record will be given after getting signature in the appropriate register.
    • Response to the court of law:
      • Requisition from the concerned party or notice from the Court of Law shall be received.
      • The same shall be forwarded to the Administrator for his approval.
      • After which a Medical Record Officer shall be made responsible for taking the original copy of the MR and replacing the same within the same day.
    • Response to other public:

Other Public agencies which approach the MR department for need of some statistics or other information’s shall be provided with the same after approval from the Administrator.

    • Release Of Information:
      • Privileged health information is used for the purposes identified or as required by law and not disclosed.
      • The MRD produces required health information to the health department as per the government order.
      • The following is the list of Reports are sent to the regulatory bodies:
Sr. No.RequirementFrequencySent To
1Notifiable disease reportOn occurrence BasisDistrict health office
2Communicable diseasesOn occurrence BasisDistrict health office
3Vaccine preventable disease Tuberculosis
Diphtheria
Pertusis

Others.		Every monthDistrict health office
4MP +ve reportsEverydayDistrict surveillance office
5HIV +ve reportsMonthlyDistrict health office
6Maternal deathsMonthlyDH&FW office
7Infant deathsmonthlyDH&FW office
      • As per the summons sent by the court of law, the required health information is released from the department without the authorization from the patient. Procedure followed is,
        • For any of the court proceedings the summons is received to the Administrator office.
        • After the approval from the Administrator, the summons is then forwarded to medical records department.
        • On the date of hearing, the requested medical record of patient is taken to the court by the authorized staff of MRD.
        • In any case if the court commissioners visit the MRD for a particular medical record, in such cases the record is hand given on submitting the summons from the court.
      • Privileged health information to insurance companies, TPA and company credit.
        • The necessary information of patients is given to the insurance companies, TPA and credit only for those patients who are claiming for the insurance and only after their authorization.
        • Requests are obtained from the various companies through Medical Superintendent of the hospital.
        • These requests are verified for patient’s authorization, given to the companies in theirs policy claim and in case of family separate authorization letter.
        • The records are sent for doctors verification against the authorization of claim provided, on obtaining this approval copy of the requested documents are attested by the treating consultant and given to the parties.
        • Certain amount of certificate charges has to be paid by the document seeker. The slip of receipt of payment is filed with request letter.
        • After providing the entries are made in the file, regarding the documents provided to the insurance claiming person.
